In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LHRH neuron population in chick is not a homogeneous population, and the migratory behavior of the individual LHRH neurons is not uniform.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LHRH neurons are able to deviate from the olfactory nerve to the trigeminal nerves, and that the LHRH neuron is able to use both the olfactory and the trigeminal neural pathways for migration.

the LHRH neuron migration is not a passive process, and the LHRH neuronal migration along the olfactory nerve and trigeminal nerves may be regulated by the interaction with the surrounding neural structures.
the migration of LIRH neurons into the trigemineal nerve bundle is not dependent on the olfactory nerve but rather on the presence of structural supports in the peripheral neural elements.

the olfactory and ophthalmic nerve bundles are not only important for guiding LHRH neurons, but also for the survival of LHRH cells.
